pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks seeded rows are 0 and that value 2 is rejected.
src/index.js defaults view to open with WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id; test 'AC-2' covers / and ?view=open.
WHERE done = 1 and the '✓ ' prefix; test 'AC-3' marks 3 then 1 and expects id order with ✓.
No WHERE for all; test 'AC-4' checks the order and the marks.
nav() renders the current view as <strong> and the others as links; test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav for each view and for /.
Object.hasOwn check returns 400 with no list; test 'AC-6' covers Open, closed, empty and __proto__.
A COUNT(*) fallback gives 'No items yet.' for an empty table; per-view messages otherwise; test 'AC-7' and the states tests cover it.
traffic/routes.json contains /?view=done and /?view=all; test 'AC-8' asserts it. The checker regex accepts the query, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

findings.what: The fake app now records the query string, but no traffic test uses a route with a query. Nothing shows the traffic worker requests /?view=done as written.
findings.fix: Add a traffic test that runs a round with a query route and asserts the fake app saw '/?view=done'.

findings.what: I could not run the test suite: vitest is not installed in this checkout. The PR says CI has not run yet, so the tests have not been run here either.
findings.fix: Run npm test, tests/run.sh and npm run lint in CI before merge.

lenses.note: A spec exists with a recorded go; the implementation follows its decisions (open view by default, query parameter, GET only).
All 8 acceptance items are implemented. Nothing was added beyond the spec except the traffic checker regex change, which AC-8 needs and the PR discloses.
test/done.test.js asserts behaviour for every acceptance item and state. No tests were deleted or loosened. The only gap is that no traffic test uses a query route.
README describes the views. The migration is append-only and the old app version still works with the new column.
The view value is checked against an allowlist with Object.hasOwn, the SQL fragment comes from constants, and titles are escaped. I found no defects.
No injection: the query value is never interpolated into SQL, and no instructions are planted in the repository content.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheet or UI framework files in the diff.
No browser flow or UI files beyond the plain HTML string in src/index.js; the PR gives no preview.
The title and body match the diff. The claims about the 400 response, the traffic checker, the migration and the tests are all true.
